_about: Rules for extensions/damage-control.ts. Deny-list of paths the delegated agent may not read, plus bash patterns it may not run. NOT a sandbox -- see README.
_attribution: Schema and 13 bash patterns derived from disler/pi-vs-claude-code (.pi/damage-control-rules.yaml), MIT (c) 2026 IndyDevDan -- https://github.com/disler/pi-vs-claude-code. Modified; see NOTICE.
_abortOnBlock: false = deny the access but let the agent continue with actionable feedback, so a delegated survey over a config dir still returns the rest of its answer. true = ctx.abort(), killing the run -- right for interactive sessions, wrong for delegation.

bashToolPatterns.reason: rm with recursive or force flags
dd writing to a raw device
brew uninstall can autoremove shared deps -- this removed node/npm once already in this repo's history
brew autoremove removes 'unneeded' formulae that other tools may depend on
curl piped to a shell (remote code execution)
base64 piped to a network tool (obfuscated egress)
adding a git remote (potential exfil target)

_rcFiles: Shell rc files moved readOnlyPaths -> zeroAccessPaths 2026-08-06. readOnlyPaths is only consulted for bash and for write/edit; read/grep/find/ls answer to zeroAccessPaths alone, so `read ~/.zshrc` was always permitted. An rc file commonly holds `export SOME_API_KEY=`, and a delegated survey has no reason to open one.
_egress: Network-egress rules added 2026-07-26. zeroAccessPaths stops a credential reaching the model; these stop project detail LEAVING the machine. Before this, 0 of 28 patterns matched any network tool.
_mcpNote: MCP config paths added 2026-07-26. brave-search-mcp carries BRAVE_API_KEY; exa and context7 are keyless. NOTE: this blocks Pi's TOOLS from reading these files -- it does NOT constrain pi-mcp-adapter itself, which loads config at extension-init, before any tool_call the guard can see.
_cookieNote: web-search.json holds pi-web-access provider keys AND the allowBrowserCookies flag that gates Chrome cookie decryption (chrome-cookies.ts: pbkdf2Sync + createDecipheriv over a copied Cookies DB). Blocking it stops the delegate reading or flipping its own browser-cookie permission. Same caveat as the MCP paths: this constrains Pi's TOOLS, not the extension's own init-time read.
